chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fazzal, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from one of his companions, who said:
I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the man who marries a woman who has insanity, vitiligo, and similar conditions. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He is responsible for the dower.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the dower if a man marries a woman with a pre-existing condition like insanity or vitiligo?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that pre-existing conditions like insanity or vitiligo do not constitute a defect warranting a reduction in the dower (*mahr*), establishing the husband as financially liable for the full amount. This ruling underscores the principle of *gharar* (uncertainty) in marriage contracts, where the husband assumes the risk of the wife's inherent traits unless otherwise specified, reflecting the Shia juristic emphasis on financial equity and contractual transparency in marital unions.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, form Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Bin Fazzal, from Abdullah Bin Bukeyr, from one of his companions who said,
‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the man who married the woman who had insanity with her, and the vitiligo, and such like. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He is responsible for the dower’.
en.sarwar: 7. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hassan ibn Ali ibn Faddal from ‘Abd Allah ibn Bukayr from certain persons of his people who has said the following: “

This is concerning my question before abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man who marries a woman who is insane or has leprosy and so on. He (the Imam) said, ‘He is responsible for mahr (dower).”’
